entries.title: New Life
entries.plain: A life begins by choosing the doctrine that will shape cultivation, preparation, combat, and eventual reincarnation.
entries.why: This entry teaches the player that path, Heart Law, Spirit Root, and early focus are not flavor labels. They define the rhythm of the current life.
entries.sect: A cultivator does not merely start a run; they accept a life.
entries.how: Open at first save, from the life-start flow, or from Records > First Steps.
entries.used: Orientation for the first hour and for every reincarnation.
mistakes: Treating the path choice as cosmetic.
Ignoring Heart Law and focus after selecting them.
Expecting the game to be only a single cultivation bar.
entries.unlock: Always visible or becomes Recorded when first encountered.
entries.jade: A life begins by choosing the doctrine that will shape cultivation, preparation, combat, and eventual reincarnation.

entries.title: First Hour
entries.plain: The first hour should teach the closed loop: cultivate Qi, inspect blockers, use the world to prepare, then challenge the first gate.
entries.why: This is the player-facing replacement for intrusive onboarding. It gives a calm sequence without forcing popups.
entries.sect: The first steps decide whether the road feels like fog or a path.
entries.how: Open from First Steps, the first Elder Note, or the Current Milestone panel.
entries.used: Early-game guidance and reincarnation orientation.
mistakes: Farming randomly without checking the next milestone.
Challenging the gate without medicine or loadout checks.
Buying manuals without knowing what slot or role they fill.
entries.unlock: Always visible or becomes Recorded when first encountered.
entries.jade: The first hour should teach the closed loop: cultivate Qi, inspect blockers, use the world to prepare, then challenge the first gate.

entries.title: What Is Cultivation?
entries.plain: Cultivation is the main inner-growth loop: gather and refine Qi, increase your cultivation base, and prepare the body and doctrine for breakthrough.
entries.why: It establishes the central fantasy and tells the player that progress also comes from support systems.
entries.sect: Cultivation is not waiting. It is the slow ordering of the body, breath, and will.
entries.how: Cultivate from the Cultivation screen. Use focus, Heart Law, and preparation systems to support progress.
entries.used: Realm advancement, breakthrough access, gate preparation, and reincarnation value.
mistakes: Thinking cultivation alone solves every wall.
Ignoring preparation because the Qi bar is full.
entries.unlock: Always visible or becomes Recorded when first encountered.
entries.jade: Cultivation is the main inner-growth loop: gather and refine Qi, increase your cultivation base, and prepare the body and doctrine for breakthrough.

entries.title: What Is Qi?
entries.plain: Qi is the primary inner progress resource. It fills through cultivation and is spent or checked when attempting breakthroughs.
entries.why: Players need to distinguish Qi from combat resources, currencies, and crafting materials.
entries.sect: Qi is breath given direction.
entries.how: Generated through cultivation, influenced by realm, substage, focus, path, Heart Law, Spirit Root, and prestige effects.
entries.used: Substage progress, breakthrough readiness, and milestone checks.
mistakes: Assuming Qi cap completion means every gate requirement is done.
Confusing Qi with currency or Spirit Stones.
entries.unlock: Always visible or becomes Recorded when first encountered.
entries.jade: Qi is the primary inner progress resource. It fills through cultivation and is spent or checked when attempting breakthroughs.

entries.title: What Is a Realm?
entries.plain: A realm is a major cultivation tier such as Qi Condensation, Foundation Establishment, Core Formation, Nascent Soul, Soul Formation, or Spirit Severing.
entries.why: Realm names define content reach, city unlocks, technique slot growth, and gate progression.
entries.sect: A realm is not a level. It is the shape of what the body can contain.
entries.how: Advance by completing substages, satisfying breakthrough requirements, and clearing or bypassing gates when needed.
entries.used: Progression, city unlocking, content gating, slot unlocking, and prestige value.
mistakes: Treating every substage as a major realm.
Expecting later city records to be live before the realm unlock exists.
entries.unlock: Always visible or becomes Recorded when first encountered.
entries.jade: A realm is a major cultivation tier such as Qi Condensation, Foundation Establishment, Core Formation, Nascent Soul, Soul Formation, or Spirit Severing.

entries.title: What Is a Substage?
entries.plain: A substage is a visible step inside a realm. Substages pace growth before a major breakthrough.
entries.why: Substages let the player understand why a breakthrough is not available yet even if progress feels close.
entries.sect: The mountain is climbed by ledges, not by a single leap.
entries.how: Cultivate Qi until each substage threshold is met.
entries.used: Breakthrough readiness, gate eligibility, and milestone tracking.
mistakes: Missing the final-substage requirement for gates.
Confusing substage completion with realm transition.
entries.unlock: Always visible or becomes Recorded when first encountered.
entries.jade: A substage is a visible step inside a realm. Substages pace growth before a major breakthrough.

entries.title: What Is a Gate?
entries.plain: A gate is a milestone threshold that tests whether cultivation, build, medicine, and preparation are sufficient for a major realm transition.
entries.why: This frames Gate Trials as readiness checks, not farms.
entries.sect: A gate does not ask if you waited. It asks if you are ready.
entries.how: Open from the World city package when the current realm and progression state make the trial relevant.
entries.used: Major breakthrough handoff and gate item acquisition.
mistakes: Treating gates as normal grind areas.
Expecting the gate item to be the entry ticket instead of the reward unless content explicitly says otherwise.
entries.unlock: Always visible or becomes Recorded when first encountered.
entries.jade: A gate is a milestone threshold that tests whether cultivation, build, medicine, and preparation are sufficient for a major realm transition.

entries.title: Why Choose a Path?
entries.plain: A path defines the life’s core playstyle: Heaven leans cultivation and spirit, Earth leans body and endurance, Martial leans combat pressure.
entries.why: Path identity affects recommendations, manual priorities, Heart Law fit, and build expectations.
entries.sect: A path is a vow about how power will be pursued.
entries.how: Chosen at life start and should remain the authoritative path for that life.
entries.used: Run identity, build guidance, Heart Law resonance, and path-aligned technique recommendations.
mistakes: Choosing a path and then ignoring its build rhythm.
Treating path mismatch as fatal; it should be suboptimal, not run-ending.
entries.unlock: Always visible or becomes Recorded when first encountered.
entries.jade: A path defines the life’s core playstyle: Heaven leans cultivation and spirit, Earth leans body and endurance, Martial leans combat pressure.

entries.title: What Is a Heart Law?
entries.plain: A Heart Law is the inner doctrine that modifies cultivation rhythm, comprehension, stability, and sometimes cross-system support.
entries.why: Players need to understand that Heart Laws are foundational and persistent within the life, not disposable spells.
entries.sect: A technique moves the hand. A Heart Law moves the self.
entries.how: Chosen or unlocked through progression, then studied through cultivation and doctrine systems.
entries.used: Cultivation modifiers, stability, comprehension, insight events, and path resonance.
mistakes: Reading Heart Law as only a passive stat card.
Ignoring resonance and breath mode.
Assuming all Heart Law effects are purely cultivation-only if the live content intentionally includes softer cross-domain synergy.
entries.unlock: Always visible or becomes Recorded when first encountered.
entries.jade: A Heart Law is the inner doctrine that modifies cultivation rhythm, comprehension, stability, and sometimes cross-system support.

entries.title: Why Did I Lose?
entries.plain: Defeat should be diagnosed as undercultivated, undergeared, underprepared, underbuilt, wrong AI profile, sustain failure, or damage failure.
entries.why: This turns combat loss into actionable routing instead of frustration.
entries.sect: A lost duel is only wasted if the lesson is not recorded.
entries.how: Opened from post-combat defeat, Gate Trial, Combat records, or Ask the Records.
entries.used: Post-loss guidance, top fixes, and routing to Forge, Apothecary, Techniques, or Cultivation.
mistakes: Retrying the same fight without changing the failed floor.
Treating every defeat as needing more Qi when the real issue may be medicine or loadout.
entries.unlock: Always visible or becomes Recorded when first encountered.
entries.jade: Defeat should be diagnosed as undercultivated, undergeared, underprepared, underbuilt, wrong AI profile, sustain failure, or damage failure.

entries.title: What Should I Do When Progress Slows?
entries.plain: When progress slows, check whether the blocker is Qi, stage, gate readiness, gear floor, medicine, build power, city reachability, or prestige timing.
entries.why: This is the player’s main anti-confusion entry.
entries.sect: A wall is either a gate, a lesson, or the end of a life.
entries.how: Open from Current Milestone, Cultivation, Status, or Ask the Records.
entries.used: Soft-wall guidance and mid-run recovery.
mistakes: Assuming slow progress means the game has no next step.
Reincarnating before checking obvious fix routes.
Pushing forever at the content cap without reading cap guidance.
entries.unlock: Always visible or becomes Recorded when first encountered.
entries.jade: When progress slows, check whether the blocker is Qi, stage, gate readiness, gear floor, medicine, build power, city reachability, or prestige timing.

entries.title: When to Reincarnate
entries.plain: Reincarnate when the current life’s marginal progress is weaker than the permanent or hybrid gains that the next life will inherit.
entries.why: This establishes prestige as a rational, legible outer-loop decision rather than a punishment.
entries.sect: A life ends. The Dao does not.
entries.how: Open from Prestige, soft-wall guidance, current content cap, or the prior-life ledger.
entries.used: Prestige timing, run summaries, AP decisions, and second-life expectations.
mistakes: Seeing reincarnation as failure.
Prestiging without understanding what resets and what remains.
Trusting prestige nodes that are not live without a clear runtime status label.
entries.unlock: Always visible or becomes Recorded when first encountered.
entries.jade: Reincarnate when the current life’s marginal progress is weaker than the permanent or hybrid gains that the next life will inherit.

entries.title: Reading the Pavilion
entries.plain: The Pavilion records explanations, relationships, current blockers, prior-life history, and source/use chains in one place.
entries.why: This teaches how to use the feature itself.
entries.sect: A jade slip is useful only when it leads the disciple back to action.
entries.how: Use categories, search, filters, Threads of Karma, Jade Slips, and Elder Notes.
entries.used: Player information literacy and onboarding to the codex.
mistakes: Reading only flavor and ignoring route buttons.
Using search only by exact names instead of sources, uses, and aliases.
entries.unlock: Always visible or becomes Recorded when first encountered.
entries.jade: The Pavilion records explanations, relationships, current blockers, prior-life history, and source/use chains in one place.

entries.title: Life Profile
entries.plain: The Life Profile summarizes path, Heart Law, Spirit Root, breath/focus mode, current realm, current city, and current milestone.
entries.why: It makes path, Heart Law, and Spirit Root read as one identity rather than disconnected labels.
entries.sect: A cultivator must know the shape of the life they are living.
entries.how: Generated from runtime state and shown in the top ribbon, Status, and Current Life category.
entries.used: Current-run diagnosis, recommendations, and prior-life comparison.
mistakes: Hiding active path and Heart Law in separate screens.
Letting stale state show multiple path truths.
entries.unlock: Always visible or becomes Recorded when first encountered.
entries.jade: The Life Profile summarizes path, Heart Law, Spirit Root, breath/focus mode, current realm, current city, and current milestone.

entries.title: Heaven Path
entries.plain: Heaven Path favors spirit, cultivation rhythm, and decisive doctrine expression. It should feel clear, bright, and efficient but less physically forgiving.
entries.why: It gives the player a cultivation/offense-forward identity with higher sensitivity to preparation.
entries.sect: Heaven seeks alignment before force.
entries.how: Chosen at life start; recommendations should favor spirit cultivation, aligned manuals, burst or scripture-oriented builds, and safe gate preparation.
entries.used: Path recommendations, manual filtering, Heart Law resonance, and build archetype classification.
mistakes: Assuming Heaven can ignore medicine or gear because cultivation is strong.
Treating it as the only correct path.
entries.unlock: Always visible or becomes Recorded when first encountered.
entries.jade: Heaven Path favors spirit, cultivation rhythm, and decisive doctrine expression. It should feel clear, bright, and efficient but less physically forgiving.

entries.title: Earth Path
entries.plain: Earth Path favors body, defense, and survival floors. It should feel patient, grounded, and resilient.
entries.why: It gives the player a defensive doctrine that values gear, medicine, and sustained fights.
entries.sect: Earth survives the strike and learns its weight.
entries.how: Chosen at life start; recommendations should favor durability, armor floor, Survivor AI, and body-support Heart Laws.
entries.used: Path recommendations, gate prep, gear floors, and defensive build templates.
mistakes: Over-investing in defense until damage becomes too low.
Ignoring technique rank because survival feels safe.
entries.unlock: Always visible or becomes Recorded when first encountered.
entries.jade: Earth Path favors body, defense, and survival floors. It should feel patient, grounded, and resilient.

entries.title: Martial Path
entries.plain: Martial Path favors active combat pressure, attack, crit, and decisive technique expression.
entries.why: It gives the player the sharpest combat rhythm and the strongest need to manage burst, accuracy, and technique timing.
entries.sect: Martial walks through the gate with a blade already moving.
entries.how: Chosen at life start; recommendations should favor weapon floor, offensive manuals, Burst or Balanced AI, and core strike mastery.
entries.used: Path recommendations, build archetypes, technique priorities, and combat diagnosis.
mistakes: Mistaking high attack for readiness if accuracy, healing, or defense is weak.
Ignoring sustain in long gate fights.
entries.unlock: Always visible or becomes Recorded when first encountered.
entries.jade: Martial Path favors active combat pressure, attack, crit, and decisive technique expression.

entries.title: Spirit Root
entries.plain: Spirit Root is the life’s innate affinity floor: it affects resonance, cultivation feel, and sometimes how strongly a doctrine blooms.
entries.why: It helps explain why some Heart Laws or paths feel more natural in a life.
entries.sect: The root is not the tree, but the tree answers it.
entries.how: Rolled, chosen, inherited, or modified by progression depending on implementation; displayed in Life Profile.
entries.used: Heart Law resonance, future prestige floor effects, and doctrinal explanation.
mistakes: Treating Spirit Root as a standalone win condition.
Hiding it after life start.
entries.unlock: Always visible or becomes Recorded when first encountered.
entries.jade: Spirit Root is the life’s innate affinity floor: it affects resonance, cultivation feel, and sometimes how strongly a doctrine blooms.

entries.title: Heart Law
entries.plain: The active Heart Law is the life’s inner scripture. It shapes cultivation, comprehension, stability, and the feel of doctrine.
entries.why: It is a foundation for both mechanical guidance and xianxia flavor.
entries.sect: A Heart Law is the handwriting of the Dao inside the body.
entries.how: Chosen at life start or unlocked through progression; studied through cultivation and chapter advancement.
entries.used: Cultivation bonuses, insight timing, chapter growth, and recommendation context.
mistakes: Treating it as an item rather than doctrine.
Not checking chapter and comprehension states.
entries.unlock: Always visible or becomes Recorded when first encountered.
entries.jade: The active Heart Law is the life’s inner scripture. It shapes cultivation, comprehension, stability, and the feel of doctrine.

entries.title: Breath Focus
entries.plain: Breath Focus prioritizes cultivation rhythm and inner refinement. It is the safest way to read a life as cultivation-first.
entries.why: Players need to understand focus modes as intentional tradeoffs.
entries.sect: Breath gathers what force scatters.
entries.how: Select from Cultivation or Life Profile if available.
entries.used: Qi generation, comprehension pacing, and inner-state recommendations.
mistakes: Leaving focus unchanged when the current blocker has changed.
Using Breath Focus when the real blocker is combat survival.
entries.unlock: Always visible or becomes Recorded when first encountered.
entries.jade: Breath Focus prioritizes cultivation rhythm and inner refinement. It is the safest way to read a life as cultivation-first.

entries.title: Body Focus
entries.plain: Body Focus prioritizes survival and physical preparation. It is most relevant when danger, HP, defense, or gate sustain is weak.
entries.why: It teaches players that body investment is a valid route to gate readiness.
entries.sect: The vessel must not crack before the Qi can settle.
entries.how: Select from Cultivation or Life Profile if available.
entries.used: Survival floor, Earth-leaning builds, defensive recovery, and gate prep.
mistakes: Using Body Focus forever after the survival problem is solved.
Assuming body focus replaces medicine or gear.
entries.unlock: Always visible or becomes Recorded when first encountered.
entries.jade: Body Focus prioritizes survival and physical preparation. It is most relevant when danger, HP, defense, or gate sustain is weak.

entries.title: Spirit Focus
entries.plain: Spirit Focus prioritizes inner clarity, comprehension, and spiritual leverage. It is strongest when doctrine growth is the bottleneck.
entries.why: It gives non-combat growth an actionable route.
entries.sect: Spirit sharpens the law before the hand moves.
entries.how: Select from Cultivation or Life Profile if available.
entries.used: Heart Law comprehension, insight preparation, and Heaven-leaning doctrine.
mistakes: Using Spirit Focus when immediate gate survival is the blocker.
Ignoring loadout and medicine while chasing insight.
entries.unlock: Always visible or becomes Recorded when first encountered.
entries.jade: Spirit Focus prioritizes inner clarity, comprehension, and spiritual leverage. It is strongest when doctrine growth is the bottleneck.

entries.title: Balanced Focus
entries.plain: Balanced Focus spreads attention across cultivation, body, and spirit. It is useful when no single bottleneck dominates.
entries.why: It gives players a default that avoids overcommitting early.
entries.sect: Balanced breath keeps the road open.
entries.how: Select from Cultivation or Life Profile if available.
entries.used: Early-life stability, general growth, and broad preparation.
mistakes: Using Balanced Focus as a way to avoid diagnosing a clear blocker.
Expecting it to outperform specialized focus against a specific wall.

entries.title: Path Resonance
entries.plain: Path Resonance is how well the active path, Heart Law, Spirit Root, techniques, and build direction support each other.
entries.why: This turns build coherence into an understandable concept.
entries.sect: When root, law, and hand agree, effort no longer leaks away.
entries.how: Displayed in Life Profile, Techniques, Heart Law, and Manual Pavilion recommendations.
entries.used: Manual recommendations, build templates, Heart Law notes, and milestone readiness.
mistakes: Treating resonance as a hard rule that forbids experimentation.
Punishing mismatch too harshly instead of guiding correction.
entries.unlock: Always visible or becomes Recorded when first encountered.
entries.jade: Path Resonance is how well the active path, Heart Law, Spirit Root, techniques, and build direction support each other.

entries.title: Doctrine Mismatch
entries.plain: Doctrine Mismatch marks a path, Heart Law, technique, or focus that works but does not strongly support the life’s active direction.
entries.why: It gives players a language for suboptimal choices without bricking runs.
entries.sect: A mismatched doctrine is not sin; it is leakage.
entries.how: Shown in recommendations, build summaries, and Heart Law notes.
entries.used: Build correction, manual selection, and path guidance.
mistakes: Calling every mismatch a failure.
Hiding mismatch until a player loses.
entries.unlock: Always visible or becomes Recorded when first encountered.
entries.jade: Doctrine Mismatch marks a path, Heart Law, technique, or focus that works but does not strongly support the life’s active direction.

entries.title: Active Doctrine

entries.why: It gives the Pavilion a stable way to summarize the current life.
entries.sect: The archive records not only what was chosen, but what the life has become.
entries.how: Generated from runtime state and shown in Current Life, Status, and prior-life summaries.
entries.used: Elder Notes, recommended records, build classification, and run summaries.

Showing build direction without the chosen doctrine.

entries.jade: Active Doctrine is the combined identity of path, Heart Law, Spirit Root, focus, loadout, and current build archetype.

generated_record_families.required_content: Generated from items.json and live source/sink resolvers. Must show name, type, rarity, source, used-for, current relevance, safe-to-sell, needed-soon, route buttons, and warnings.
Generated from alchemy recipe content. Must show station, inputs, output, unlock, craft time, best source for missing inputs, and used-for.
Generated from forge blueprint content. Must show required materials, output gear/tool, floor impact, missing sources, and gate relevance.
Generated from technique content. Must show path alignment, active/passive/ultimate slot, role, source manual, mastery/rank, traits, rune sockets, AI fit, and current milestone value.
Generated from manual content and Manual Pavilion pools. Must show grade, path/family, technique output, duplicate conversion, study time, and current build gap relevance.
Generated from Heart Law content plus authored doctrine intro. Must show doctrine, chapters, bonuses, resonance, breath mode fit, and live/inactive effect status.
Generated from cities.json plus authored summaries. Must show unlockMajorRealm, modules, refs, gate, ruin, manual pools, role, reachability, and content-cap state.
Generated from trials.json, trial lifecycle, gate resolver, and fail-safe normalization. Must show eligibility, gate reward, fail-safe, readiness, clear/bypass/defeat state.
Generated from ruins content. Must show route identity, encounters, deterministic rewards, drought solved, recommended prep, and city relation.
Generated from enemies content and encounter history. Must show first-seen/defeated/mastered, threat tags, drops, counters, and best source connections.
Generated from rune content. Must show socket type, effect, source, compatible techniques/items, and build fit.
Generated from talisman content. Must show craft inputs, output, effect, duration/trigger, source, and situational use.
Generated from bounty templates. Must show target, difficulty, reward, Merit value, route, and current relevance.
Generated from prestige_store.json and runtime-applied effects. Must show cost, prerequisites, live/inactive status, effect, reset/retain impact, and advisor relevance.
